mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Shareholder Certificate of Identity (Passport Copy, Notarized)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent Authority in Country of Origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Non-User of Prohibited Names

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against Luxembourg Financial Sector Supervisory Commission (CSSF) regulations, EU Council Sanctions Lists, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, and domestic PEP registers. Enhanced due diligence required for any politically exposed person, beneficial owner, or shareholder with a direct or indirect interest above 25%, using a risk-based approach compliant with the revised Law of 12 November 2004.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS Luxembourg)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate names must be submitted in at least one of Luxembourg's official languages (French, German, Luxembourgish) or in a recognized Latin-script transliteration. The name must include the full corporate form 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL'. A name may include other languages provided transliteration is supplied and the name is not misleading. Any name containing the terms 'bank', 'assurance', 'fiduciary', 'investment fund', 'état', 'commune', or 'european institution' requires prior ministerial or regulatory approval.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may submit a written administrative appeal to the RCS Registrar within fifteen days of the rejection notice. The appeal must include the proposed name, a legal justification, and evidence of non-conflicting use. The RCS Registrar must issue a decision within ten business days. A further judicial appeal may be lodged with the Luxembourg District Court within two months of the second rejection. Name reservations may be renewed once for a further 30-day period prior to expiry, subject to payment of a renewed reservation fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office in Luxembourg may be accepted for administrative and correspondence purposes only; it does not constitute a physical registered office for statutory requirements. For the IP patent prosecution agency industry (ISIC 7490), CSSF and RCS practice require a genuine substance presence. A physical address, local correspondence capacity, and substantive local oversight are mandatory for obtaining and maintaining the required professional license.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (probability 0.8) – Unannounced on-site inspections by CSSF and RCS are common within the first 12 months of operation for licensed professional service providers, particularly those active in intellectual property prosecution and international trademark registration.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Amended Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, Articles 710-1 to 710-24 (SARL); Grand-Ducal regulations on the Register of Commerce and Societies and company publication obligations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Luxembourg
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif reçu par notaire) together with the electronic RCS filing and publication notice in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum share capital for a standard SARL under the amended Law of 10 August 1915, unless a higher amount is fixed in the articles. All subscribed shares must be fully paid up in cash before execution of the notarial deed. The contribution may be deposited in a Luxembourg credit institution account in the Company's name, or with a notary's escrow account or the Caisse de Consignation, and remains blocked until registration as confirmed by a bank certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporator and sole shareholder approves the draft articles of association, subscribes all shares at EUR [●] aggregate par value, and declares such capital is fully paid up and evidenced by the notary's bank certificate. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Company's registered office is established at [●] in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg. FURTHER RESOLVED, that [●] is appointed sole manager with authority to open bank accounts, sign, conduct tax and administrative filings, and represent the Company before the RCS and all competent authorities. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the manager be and is authorised to execute and deliver any patent and trademark regulatory documents and to cause the incorporation to be published in the RESA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation due diligence, name clearance and article drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chosen Luxembourg notary; RCS name database made available through Luxembourg Business Registers (lbr.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Check the proposed corporate name in the RCS availability data, verify director/shareholder suitability, and cause the notary to prepare the articles of association in French or German with an English translation for KYC purposes. Obtain the registered office address consent and complete AML/KYC onboarding information before the notarial appointment.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association compliant with the Law of 10 August 1915
Identification documents of all shareholders and the future manager
AML/KYC forms, beneficial ownership structure and business plan
Proposed corporate name availability record or extraction
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or availability is challenged, submit an alternative distinctive name or file a reasoned objection with the notary; an arbitrary administrative refusal may be challenged before the competent administrative tribunal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of share capital bank account and payment or certification of subscribed capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A Luxembourg credit institution; alternatively the notary's escrow account or the Caisse de Consignation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional company bank account in the name of the prospective SARL, deposit the full subscribed capital, and obtain a banker's certificate confirming the funds are available and reserved for the Company. Deliver the certificate to the notary no later than the day of execution of the deed.
required_dossiers: Draft articles containing the capital schedule
Bank account application forms and AML/KYC declarations
Identification and beneficial ownership documentation of subscribers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays KYC or account opening, place the capital on the notary's statutory escrow account or with the Caisse de Consignation and obtain a deposit certificate acceptable for the notarial deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the notarial deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary domiciled in Luxembourg admitted to the Chambre des notaires du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All subscribers appear before the notary, physically or by valid power of attorney. The notary verifies the identity of the parties, the bank certificate and the legality of the articles, reads the deed, and records the signatures. The notary then issues the authentic deed and certified extracts needed for the RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Notarial incorporation deed draft prepared by the notary
Bank certificate or escrow deposit certificate for the subscribed capital
Registered office lease or written consent of the property owner
Valid passports, powers of attorney and tax identification numbers of the parties
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any inconsistency is discovered before execution, the deed is held and corrected through a revised notarial draft; clerical errors after signature are rectified by means of a supplemental deed or confidential erratum filed with the RCS before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration and publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) through the Luxembourg Business Registers e-filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the certified notarial deed, registered office details, manager information and specimen signatures electronically with the RCS. Once validated, the RCS assigns the Company registration number and triggers publication in the RESA, thereby conferring legal personality and opposability to third parties.
required_dossiers: Authentic notarial deed and certified RCS extract request
Registered office lease or owner consent
Manager's identity, curriculum vitae where requested, and specimen signature form
Declaration of non-disqualification and absence of pending bankruptcy proceedings
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS queries the filing, remedy the query within fifteen calendar days through the notary using the online LBR portal; a manifest refusal may be appealed before the Luxembourg District Court in commercial matters, with the Company or notary as applicant.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, social security and national business register activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the newly incorporated SARL in the national EIN/registration system, apply for a Luxembourg corporate income tax reference and VAT number where applicable, and register as employer with the CCSS. The registered office and RCS certificate are used to evidence commencement of the commercial activity.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate and extract
Notarial deed of incorporation
Registered office lease and occupation certificate
Manager identification and formal tax/social declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VAT or tax number issuance is delayed, submit an AE/VAT income declaration at the AEDT counter citing the RCS registration date; administrative delay is cured by mandatory registration and may be escalated by formal reminder to the competent directorate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Beneficial owner registration, governance authorizations and sector permit applications
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE) maintained by Luxembourg Business Registers; Ministry of Economy for establishment licensing where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the beneficial ownership (UBO) declaration in the RBE within the statutory deadline, adopt written resolutions approving the appointment of the manager and opening of business accounts, and, where the patent prosecution agency qualifies as a commercial activity, submit the business establishment permit application to the Ministry of Economy. Maintain the legal and accounting records at the registered office.
required_dossiers: RBE beneficial ownership declaration form and UBO identity evidence
Written resolutions of the sole shareholder and manager appointment
RCS extract and certified copy of the articles
Business establishment permit application where the activity qualifies as a regulated commercial activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the UBO filing is queried, resubmit the structure chart and legal ownership documents; any late filing penalty can be mitigated by a supplementary declaration in the RBE portal. Refusal of a permit is subject to administrative appeal before the Ministry of Economy.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie, Direction générale PME – Service des autorisations d'établissement
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement / business establishment permit for the regulated commercial operation of a professional services agency

environmental_impact_assessment.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement – Ministère de l'Environnement, du Climat et du Développement durable
environmental_impact_assessment.classification_tier: Exempt from full Environmental Impact Assessment; office-based intellectual property agency with no significant industrial installation. Administrative environmental registration may apply only if physical printing, warehouse storage or a small data installation is added.
environmental_impact_assessment.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process emissions; domestic sewage and sanitary effluents compliant with the Loi modifiée du 19 décembre 2008 relative à l'eau, VOCs and printing emissions below de minimis thresholds; paper and electronic confidential records transferred only through authorised waste collectors in accordance with Luxembourg waste regulation and EU Regulation No 1013/2006.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance obtained from the communal fire prevention authority for the registered office, structural load assessment where archival or storage fit-out exceeds normal office loading, and occupational health conformity assessed by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) with emergency evacuation arrangements and first-aid equipment in place.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; unified government e-administration portal: guichet.lu / MyGuichet.lu; e-filing platforms: eCDF and SOFIA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Luxembourg SARL obtains its statutory tax matricule automatically upon notarial incorporation and registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers / RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés); the matricule serves as the corporate income tax TIN. VAT registration with the AEDT is mandatory within 15 days of commencing taxable activities and is filed through MyGuichet.lu (eTVA Form 1040) or in paper form, producing a Luxembourg TVA identification number. A foreign entity without a Luxembourg fixed establishment that makes taxable supplies or incurs VAT in Luxembourg must appoint a Luxembourg VAT representative and register for VAT; a foreign entity with a fixed establishment must register both the establishment in the RCS and obtain a Luxembourg matricule plus VAT ID before supplying services. No minimum capital or local director condition is imposed solely for VAT registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the SARL is an opaque tax-resident corporation subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) and net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune), taxed on worldwide income with participation exemption relief and no pass-through eligibility.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not apply a US-style check-the-box regime; SARL classification is fixed by law as opaque. Available elections include: (i) fiscal unity / tax consolidation election under Article 164bis LIR for CIT and municipal business tax; (ii) participation exemption election for qualifying dividends and capital gains (10% holding or EUR 1.2 million acquisition cost and 12-month holding period); (iii) 80% IP box exemption election under Article 50bis LIR for qualifying patent and software IP income, subject to the nexus ratio; (iv) VAT grouping election under Article 60 of the VAT Law; (v) ATAD / anti-hybrid mismatch rules (Law of 21 December 2018) are mandatory self-assessed adjustments rather than elective mechanisms.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT — Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée (Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979, as amended, transposing EU Directive 2006/112/EC)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold for domestic taxable persons — a SARL must register for VAT from the first euro of taxable activity. An optional small-enterprise exemption (franchise) applies under Article 57 of the VAT Law only while annual turnover does not exceed EUR 30,000, with the right to opt into regular taxation. For intra-EU distance sales of goods, the Union-wide threshold of EUR 10,000 applies; B2B services follow place-of-supply rules and are wholly outside the domestic registration threshold framework.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None — Luxembourg currently imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, no mandatory API-based exchange, and no digital stamping regime for B2B VAT invoices. Mandatory B2G e-invoicing applies to public contracts through the Luxembourg public procurement platform using PEPPOL / Peppol BIS 3.0 and EN 16931 data model. Electronic storage of invoices is permitted provided authenticity and integrity are guaranteed by EDI, digital signature, or PEPPOL compliant transmission. VAT invoices must be issued no later than the 15th day of the month following the month of supply. The EU ViDA framework is expected to introduce general mandatory e-invoicing, but not before 2030/2035.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Patent prosecution services supplied by a Luxembourg SARL to an EU taxable person are subject to the reverse charge with Luxembourg VAT at 0% (place of supply in the customer's Member State under Article 43 of the VAT Law / Article 44 of the EU VAT Directive), and must be reported in the EC Sales List. Services supplied to non-EU taxable persons fall outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT, provided the customer's business status is evidenced. Physical exports of goods, including certified file copies and sample dossiers, are zero-rated under Article 53 of the VAT Law when proof of the outward customs declaration is retained; intra-EU dispatches are zero-rated where the customer's VAT ID is valid and transmitted. Official patent office fees reimbursed strictly on behalf of a client may be excluded from the taxable base as disbursements under Article 45 of the VAT Law where the SARL acts in a disclosed agency capacity, including for PCT, EPO and WIPO filings. All documentary evidence must be complete before the return filing deadline; otherwise the supply is recharacterised as taxable at 17%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD / PLATO ICS declaration) — required solely for physical exports of goods, samples or certified file copies
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill (carrier-issued transport evidence for physical export)
Signed Service Agreement and Engagement Letter (evidence of B2B service supply and place of supply)
Customer's Validated EU VAT ID and VIES confirmation printout (for intra-EU reverse charge)
Overseas Customer Business Registration Certificate, Tax Residency Certificate, or equivalent proof of foreign taxable status (for non-EU services)
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT payment evidence showing collection of export proceeds on bank records
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may retrospectively claw back the unwound VAT and issue a deficiency assessment on any export zero-rating claim lacking satisfactory evidence, within the general five-year limitation period, extended to ten years where fraud is established. Unpaid VAT attracts statutory late-payment interest compounded monthly; administrative fines of up to EUR 10,000 per infringement may be imposed for faulty or incomplete documentation. Deliberate fraudulent export zero-rating supported by forged invoices, false customs declarations, or fabricated foreign payment evidence constitutes tax fraud under Luxembourg law, punishable by fines up to EUR 75,000 and imprisonment of up to five years pursuant to the General Tax Law (Abgabenordnung). Luxembourg maintains no exchange-control restrictions; the 180-day repatriation benchmark reflects the internal documentary and treaty-mapping control requirement for the patent prosecution fee cycle rather than a statutory currency-control deadline.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (Central Bank of Luxembourg)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible in Luxembourg; no general exchange control or foreign exchange licensing regime applies to current or capital transactions. The EU Treaty and OECD liberalisation codes govern cross-border movements, with profit remittances permitted after annual accounts approval and board shareholder distribution decision. Non-resident profit remittances are legally unrestricted, although Luxembourg dividend withholding tax of 15% applies at statutory rate and may be reduced under applicable double tax treaties. No separate convertibility approval is required for patent prosecution agency fees, client remittances, royalty streams, or intercompany settlement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg maintains no statutory export proceeds surrender obligation, mandatory conversion percentage, or repatriation timeline. Export and service receipts may be retained freely in euro or in any foreign currency in a resident or non-resident bank account. Regulatory balance-of-payments reporting to the Banque centrale du Luxembourg may apply to cross-border flows for statistical purposes, but no conversion or surrender duty exists.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-High for operational disbursements and low-value official patent office wire transfers; Medium for general FX transparency. Luxembourg and EU/EEA Electronic Money Institutions with a valid MiFID/EMD licence and PSD2 passport may onboard the SARL remotely, subject to Luxembourg AML/CFT law. Such EMIs can provide payment accounts and cross-border settlement rails, including SEPA and Wise-style services, but generally cannot provide credit or serve as escrow providers for regulated client funds. A licensed bank remains advisable for capital escrow, large cross-border receipts, documentary credits, and long-term treasury lines.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is legally possible under the Luxembourg AML/CFT Law of 12 November 2004, as amended, using electronic identification, qualified electronic signatures, and videoconference KYC procedures. In practice, Tier-1 banks frequently require at least one physical attendance or a notarised/consular identification for foreign directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners. All directors and UBOs must undergo individual identity verification, source-of-wealth assessment, and business rationale review. The bank's internal KYC policy dictates whether remote opening is permissible without a physical interview; for this SARL a hybrid approach is recommended: notarised corporate documents plus one physical or videoconference meeting for the director and UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity or multi-jurisdictional corporate chain masking the identity of the ultimate beneficial owner
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid passports of all UBOs and directors, Luxembourg RCS extract, Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) extract, constitutional documents, deed of incorporation, shareholders' register, a clear corporate structure chart showing each intermediary company, evidence of commercial substance in Luxembourg, and a written business-purpose narrative for the IP patent prosecution agency structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cross-border wires to official patent offices, foreign trademark registries, and client counsel without observable commercial justification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed professional services agreements, itemised fee schedules, PCT/EPO/WIPO filing references, official tariff sheets, client mandates and powers of attorney, historical invoice/receipt pairs, list of adjudicated official patent office fees, and annual revenue projection aligned with the IP prosecution business model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payment structures where patent prosecution fees are paid on behalf of foreign clients or beneficial owners located in non-EU jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinions on client onboarding under ISO 19600/AML frameworks, proof of client identity and ultimate beneficial ownership, written client instructions, fully reconciled third-party payment schedules, executed client agreements, deposit account agreements for holding client funds, and declaration that the SARL does not disguise a foreign financial institution.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound share capital injections and shareholder contributions should be routed by SWIFT MT103 from the ultimate parent or funding bank. The compliant wire instruction should include ISO 20022 purpose code EQUI (equity investment) or, for shareholder loans, GENR/CORP/CLEAN among permissible counterparty purpose codes. The beneficiary message must identify the SARL by exact legal name and Luxembourg IBAN, with a narrative citing the notarial deed of incorporation, share capital subscription, or capital increase resolution. Verification required by the receiving bank includes the notarised deed, updated RCS/EBR extract, UBO declaration, and confirmation that the capital is booked on a Luxembourg bank account. Cross-border direct investment transactions are reportable for Banque centrale du Luxembourg balance-of-payments statistical purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for global patent prosecution and trademark registration must use bank-grade clearing rails. SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) is used for euro-denominated payments within the EEA, including official fees to European Patent Office, EUIPO, national patent offices, and foreign trademark registries. SWIFT MT103 is used for non-SEPA disbursements and any currency other than EUR. Commercial documentary letters of credit (MT700/MT707) are appropriate only for ancillary trade settlements, never for statutory official fees. The SARL may also use the WIPO Current Account mechanism for international filings. For client-prosecution expense disbursements, the clearing instruction should reference the PCT application number, WIPO reference, or corresponding invoice line, and must be mirrored in the supporting transfer-pricing transactional documentation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) only for counterparty currencies subject to external convertibility restrictions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of approved annual accounts (comptes annuels) with the business register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual General Meeting within 6 months of financial year end; accounts deposit within 7 months of financial year end (e.g., 31 July for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-imposed fines on request of the Public Prosecutor; continued non-filing can lead to administrative strike-off or dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership (RBE declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Once per calendar year; electronic confirmation window between 1 January and 1 September
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 10,000; criminal sanctions for knowingly false confirmations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (déclaration de l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due 31 May following the tax year; extensions may be granted where accounts are approved after that date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest of 0.6% per month; late-filing penalty up to EUR 25,000; provisional assessment on estimated income

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal business tax return (déclaration de l'impôt commercial communal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) on behalf of the commune
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due 31 May following the tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest and penalty up to EUR 25,000; reassessment after same due process as income tax

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Net wealth tax return (déclaration de l'impôt sur la fortune)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due 31 May following the tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest; penalty up to EUR 25,000; minimum net wealth tax automatically assessed

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if the SARL exceeds two of three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million; net turnover EUR 8.8 million; 50 average employees. Exemptions apply for certain small companies and non-public-interest entities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 on commercial register and accounting; IFRS as adopted by the EU required for consolidated financial statements of groups whose securities are listed.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must confirm the data of all beneficial owners once per calendar year in the RBE before 1 September. Shareholding transfers recorded in the register of members must be reflected in the confirmed UBO data; any mid-year ownership change also requires a separate updated declaration within the statutorily prescribed filing window.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Managers (registre des gérants et administrateurs)
Minute Book of Shareholders' Resolutions and Board Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $12,000 – $30,000 (if the size-based audit threshold is exceeded)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% CIT base rate (Luxembourg corporate income tax) plus 7% solidarity surcharge on CIT; combined CIT 18.19% before municipal business tax; aggregate effective headline in Luxembourg City approximates 24.94% including municipal business tax.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP (patent box) regime: 80% exemption of qualifying net IP income from corporate income tax and municipal business tax, yielding an effective maximum tax burden of approximately 5.21% for qualifying licensed/derived patent income; participation exemption for substantial qualifying shareholdings (≥10% or ≥EUR 6M purchase cost, held 12 months, and comparable taxation), exempting dividends and capital gains; investment tax credit and ACE-like interest deduction mechanics are not part of Luxembourg’ standard regime.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Luxembourg corporate income tax return Form 550 (Formulaire 550) filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu portal / eTax system; separate municipal business tax return also embedded with the same Form 550 filing package.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The statutory deadline is 31 May of the year following the fiscal year-end; this deadline is extended by operation of law for returns filed electronically by a certified tax advisor, and further specific extensions may be granted in writing by the Luxembourg tax office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross business revenue from patent prosecution services, PCT filing agency fees, trademark registration revenue, and ancillary IP consultancy fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident patent agency SARL must report only Luxembourg-source income and income attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment; exclude foreign-source fee income derived through genuine foreign economic activity without a Luxembourg nexus.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 112 / Cost of Sales and Gross Margin
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct professional fees, official patent office filing fees, translation costs, technical search costs, and direct online service charges attributable to rendered IP prosecution services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses directly connected to Luxembourg PE income; intra-group shared costs must satisfy arm's length transfer pricing documentation and economic substance benchmarks.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit before extraordinary items, after deducting administrative expenses, employee payroll, office overheads, depreciation, and professional fees from the gross margin.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident SARL must apply Luxembourg commercial law accounting rules and the CIR (LIR) deduction rules; transfer pricing adjustments with related parties must be properly documented in local file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 130 / IP Income Deduction (IP Box Declaration)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net qualifying income derived from qualifying patent/IP assets, after caveats from the 80% IP regime exemption; attach detailed IP nexus fraction and asset tracking records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only IP assets developed or economically held through the Luxembourg entity qualify; a foreign parent or non-resident beneficial owner requiring mere passive registration without functional personnel/premises will trigger the economic substance and anti-avoidance denial rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmed taxable amount after application of IP exemption, participation exemption, and all legal deductions; used for calculation of CIT, surcharge, and municipal business tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpayer must ensure any treaty allocation and PE attribution are accurately reflected in this box; incomplete attribution may invoke the deemed PE rules and full Luxembourg taxation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: automatic summons and tax assessment ex officio; late payment interest accrues monthly at 0.8% on underpaid CIT. Wilfull non-filing triggers a statutory criminal fine and administrative penalty up to EUR 250,000 plus, in aggravated cases, criminal indictment and director-level liability.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% on Luxembourg-source dividends paid by a Luxembourg SARL to a non-resident corporate or individual shareholder; 0% applies under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the parent holds at least 10% of share capital, plus 0% under Luxembourg participation exemption for controlling shareholders meeting holding-period and comparable-taxation requirements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced or nil rate under an applicable Luxembourg DTA, the non-resident shareholder must hold a Luxembourg Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) for its own tax residence in the treaty jurisdiction and provide a duly completed TRC release form (Form 8Q) with the application. The relevant withholding tax is initially charged at the 15% domestic rate; refund application or advance clearance through Luxembourg withholding tax procedure must be submitted and supported by the TRC, legal ownership proof, and, where applicable, the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive certification.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic WHT: 0% on outbound royalties paid by a Luxembourg SARL to non-residents (no Luxembourg withholding tax applies to pure patent royalties); 0% on normal arm's length interest on loans (subject to anti-arbitrage and profit-participating loan exceptions). Treaty rates: generally ranged 0%–10% for royalties and 0%–10% for interest, depending on the creditor's treaty residence; EU Interest & Royalties Directive normally secures 0% WHT for related companies meeting the 25% (effective 3%?) direct qualification, as transposed in Luxembourg domestic law.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File obligation triggers where the Luxembourg entity belongs to a multinational group with consolidated group revenue exceeding EUR 350 million; Local File obligation triggers where the Luxembourg entity's own annual turnover exceeds EUR 50 million. Transactions with related parties below these thresholds still require contemporaneous benchmarking evidence and a DESC-compliant TP file if the tax inspector requests it based on transaction value and risk profile.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply a pure offshore ESR like Cayman/Caribbean regimes, but a full economic substance doctrine applies under general anti-abuse rules, the OECD BEPS nexus approach for IP regimes, and Luxembourg court doctrine requiring the actual exercise of senior management, strategic decision-making, personnel, premises, and own equipment to obtain treaty and directive benefits. A patent prosecution SARL must therefore demonstrate face-to-face client intake, patent drafting control, substantive PTO interactions, and commercial risk absorption in Luxembourg.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission or undervaluation of revenue from US/EU patent office fee reimbursement, PCT search fee margin, or IP licensing income; artificial diversion of fees to shell non-resident associates while the Luxembourg SARL survives on nominal margin.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Financial penalty up to EUR 250,000 or three times the evaded tax; additional 0.8% monthly late-payment interest; civil restitution of all due Luxembourg CIT and municipal business tax; criminal fine and possible seizure of assets in amounts equivalent to concealed taxable base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil under Luxembourg law and joint/several liability of directors for corporate tax debts caused by intentional wrongful acts; travel bans, temporary ban on commercial activities, personal bankruptcy sanction, and imprisonment up to 2 years for conviction of tax fraud and up to 5 years for aggravated fraud by use of false instruments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registering a Luxembourg SARL title to IP patents and signed patent filing contracts, but without any actual professional staff, physical office, local management, or client contact; using the SARL solely as an invoicing pass-through for Cayman or zero-tax jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Revocation of IP regime benefits; denial of tax treaty relief and EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive; 80% IP deduction recompute with back taxes, penalties equal to 10%–50% of the recalculated taxable amount, and consequential domestic withholding tax assessments at 15% on deemed distributions; administrative closure of the company and removal of the Chamber of Commerce registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and formally appointed managers face civil restitution orders; a personal prohibition on business activity and/or withdrawal of the required professional license for patent prosecution; criminal prosecution for fiscal evasion with imprisonment up to 5 years and fines of up to EUR 150,000 where the vehicle is used for tax abuse.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive service/patent outsourcing fees to a non-resident affiliated IP owner leaving less than 2% net margin in the Luxembourg SARL; unsupported comparable; absence of Local File/Master File despite EUR 50M/350M thresholds; unwillingness to produce contemporaneous documentation on inspection.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment reallocating taxable income to Luxembourg with 5.21% IP-box or 24.94% standard CIT; late-interest monthly at 0.8%; administrative fine up to EUR 20,000 per missing documentation set; denial of deductible payments and withholding tax applied to deemed dividend or quasi-dividend distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Senior managers are personally liable for the corporate tax adjustments resulting from intentional false documentation or for failure to maintain statutory records; the Commercial Court may issue a seizure order against directors' personal assets and order disqualification of technical signatory rights for the patent agency license.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing high-volume patent fees through the SARL account from unidentified beneficial owners, including silent partners from sanctioned jurisdictions; client due diliedgence files missing on PCT official fee wires; involvement in laundering proceeds through payments to shell associates, use of Wise in countries prohibited by EU AML CRR.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine up to EUR 2 million against legal persons; disgorgement of proceeds; closure of client account banking; criminal fine of up to EUR 1.25 million per act; criminal sanctions for non-disclosure to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU). Critical note: patent prosecution agencies, though low-risk, are obligated professionals under the revised CSSF AML law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and beneficial owners face deprivation of liberty from 6 months to 5 years for money laundering complicity; a travel ban and 21st century version of banishment within Schengen can be imposed upon arraignment; professional mandate permanently removed by the IP professional chamber registration body; personal restitution equal to all laundered fee values.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File Tax Return / Non-Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: No submission of Form 550 for two consecutive years despite active patent prosecution revenue flow; ignoring official automatic tax assessment; use of non-resident address while maintaining economic activity physically impossible to assess.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative ex officio assessment without deductions, triggering 100% tax jurisdiction over worldwide income in absence of treaty declaration; penalty charge of 10% of assessed tax (minimum EUR 100) plus late-filing fine up to EUR 1,000 per missing year; irreversible forfeiture of IP regime exemptions due to failure to claim in the filed return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Statutorily mandatory director declaration: failing to approve and sign returns exposes directors to direct recovery under Luxembourg insolvency rules; judges may imposing a 3-year travel ban and EUR 50,000 civil sanction; criminal contempt verdict in the administrative court grants 60-day default penalty ordering the company to comply and, additionally, temporary custody of managing director in severe habitual violations.
